summary: The mayor owns the mistake in plain words, says what they assumed, apologizes to the people affected, and says what will change.
realLife: Mayors apologizing at council meetings or to the press used few words and gave no excuse. One said what she had assumed and apologized to the people who did the work; one said he overstepped his role; one said she should not have raised her voice and used profanity, but would not step down from her committee post.
sources: Erica Stewart, San Luis Obispo mayor, statement apologizing for how a grand jury report was handled (as reported by KSBY): https://www.ksby.com/san-luis-obispo/san-luis-obispo-mayor-apologizes-over-handling-of-confidential-grand-jury-report-release
Mike Signer, Charlottesville mayor, statement apologizing for overstepping his role, Aug 30, 2017: https://augustafreepress.com/news/charlottesville-mayor-issues-apology-critical-comments/

Gina Ortiz Jones, San Antonio mayor, press conference apologizing to a council colleague, Feb 24, 2026 (Texas Public Radio): https://www.tpr.org/government-politics/2026-02-24/mayor-jones-issues-public-apology-as-san-antonio-city-council-prepares-for-censure-vote
Read by the local and campaign speeches writer's helper, Nov 24, 2026; some pages were read in part or through a page summary, and every description is a paraphrase.
